thread:
maya: mock attached — trying two patterns for schema result cards' action affordances. TL;DR: compact inline buttons vs overflow action drawer. Which should be the default? https://figma.com/file/zzz :thinking_face:

sam: I lean compact for quick scanning, but keyboard discoverability is a concern. if compact, we need a visible keyboard target for the overflow menu.

kevin: product side — customers with many tools want consistent placement. default should minimize cognitive load.

aria: a11y note: compact buttons ok but must meet 44px hit target and have clear aria-labels. overflow drawer needs focus trap + announce on open.

maya: good points @aria. my current proposal: compact primary action visible + overflow for secondary. show a subtle keyboard hint on hover. thoughts? :eyes:

sam: agree. tiny copy nit: use `Invoke` rather than `Run` in primary CTA — we use `Invoke` across tool flows.

kevin: +1 for consistent terminology. also add a tooltip: "Invoke tool — preserves schema args" to reduce confusion.

maya: updated mock and added a tiny keyboard helper. pasted snippet for the help text we could show in the shortcut overlay:
```
Shortcut: K then Enter -> focus primary action
Esc -> close action drawer
```

aria: also ensure overflow uses role="menu" and that screenreader announces "X actions available" when opened. verify with VoiceOver/JAWS.

design-bot: quick poll started — vote for default pattern: compact-inline, expanded-drawer, or hybrid (primary visible + overflow). React to vote below.

sam: :thumbsup: compact-inline

kevin: :point_right: hybrid

aria: :white_check_mark: expanded-drawer (accessibility-first)

maya: thanks y'all. plan: run a 1k-session A/B comparing compact-inline vs hybrid (since hybrid hits both dev/product goals) and measure: CTR on primary, avg time-to-invoke, keyboard-success-rate, and SR accessibility errors. I'll share test plan + metrics Monday.

sam: can we include microcopy variants in the experiment? `Invoke` vs `Run` + tooltip phrasing.

maya: yes — adding two copy arms. filing follow-up doc in product drive and will link it here.

kevin: ops note — include cost-per-invocation from infra so we can weigh UX lift vs token cost.

maya: noted, pinging @kevin for metric ids and tagging infra.

sam: perfect. thanks everyone — excited to see results.
